parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.question_text: State Newton’s third law of motion.
parts.question_text_latex: State Newton’s third law of motion.

parts.label: (b)
parts.question_text:
Two spheres approach one another along a line joining their centres, as illustrated in
Fig. 3.1.
When they collide, the average force acting on sphere A is F_{A} and the average force
acting on sphere B is F_{B}.
The forces act for time t_{A} on sphere A and time t_{B} on sphere B.
parts.question_text_latex:
Two spheres approach one another along a line joining their centres, as illustrated in
Fig. 3.1.
When they collide, the average force acting on sphere A is $F_{\mathrm{A}}$ and the average force
acting on sphere B is $F_{\mathrm{B}}$.
The forces act for time $t_{\mathrm{A}}$ on sphere A and time $t_{\mathrm{B}}$ on sphere B.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.question_text:
State the relationship between
1. F_{A} and F_{B},
2. t_{A} and t_{B}.
parts.question_text_latex:
State the relationship between
1. $F_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $F_{\mathrm{B}}$,
2. $t_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $t_{\mathrm{B}}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.question_text:
Use your answers in (i) to show that the change in momentum of sphere A is equal
in magnitude and opposite in direction to the change in momentum of sphere B.

in magnitude and opposite in direction to the change in momentum of sphere B.
